sun.upright:
Look at the figure on this card, two coins in play and one foot off the ground, and then think about how an Aries Sun likes to work. You want one big thing, done first and done by you. The Two of Pentacles hands you two, and asks you to keep both going without either one getting the whole of you. Capricorn, the card's sign, squares Aries. Both are cardinal, both are starters, and a square between two starters is friction that makes something happen, usually because neither will wait for the other.

Jupiter is the planet behind this card, and in Aries it has no rank of its own, so it picks up Mars's habits. That makes the card's appetite competitive. You don't take on the second job or the extra project because you need it. You take it on to show you can, and you'll mostly manage it, which is the dangerous part. From the inside it feels like being alive, both coins moving, the day full. Then comes the Thursday when both need you at the same hour and you realise you never decided which one comes first.

At work this is the role plus the side thing, or two managers who each think they have first call on you. With money it's the new venture paid for out of the account that was meant for the car. Your body runs on bursts and flags mid-afternoon, and earth, the card's element, neither feeds fire nor fights it, so the steadiness has to be brought in on purpose. Each morning, before you check anything, say which of the two gets you first if they clash.
sun.reversed:
Pride is usually what tips this over for an Aries Sun. You said yes to both, you said it quickly, and backing out of one feels like losing. So you keep both coins going with gritted teeth, and the Mars colouring on Jupiter turns the juggle into a fight with your own diary. The other way it goes is boredom. The balancing gets tedious, and you drop one coin on purpose, loudly, just to feel something decisive happen.

Work is usually first to feel it, as the project you started with a flourish and quietly handed back half done, or a deadline you're racing that you set yourself. A partner sees it in plans cancelled at short notice because something came up, again. Money shows it as the overdraft you meant to clear last month. Pick the commitment you'd be least sorry to lose and give it back cleanly, with a proper handover and no speech about it.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon feels a thing and wants to do something about it straight away, and this card asks for the harder trick of holding two feelings at once without acting on either. Annoyed with your partner and fond of them. Excited about the offer and dreading what it'll cost. The Two keeps both coins moving, and for a Moon ruled by Mars that feels a bit like being told to sit on your hands.

Jupiter is only visiting Aries, with no dignity there, and it picks up the host's temperature, so your moods run big and fast when this card turns up. Capricorn squares your Moon, and the feeling of that square is a hand on your shoulder at the exact moment you were about to send the message. Earth and fire don't clash and don't help each other either, so the slow, bodily steadiness this card is about has to be brought to your temper deliberately. You'll know the state, pacing the kitchen at eleven at night, pulled between the two, wanting one of them to just win.

Sleep is where it goes when the day doesn't settle it, waking with a jolt and a list. With a sibling or an old friend, it's the argument you want to have and the peace you also want to keep. And there's energy in your body that needs spending before you can think straight. Go for a hard walk or a run in the middle of the day, and leave the decision about which feeling wins until you're back and your heart rate's down.
moon.reversed:
With the card upside down, an Aries Moon gets snappy from switching. Too many small demands, each one pulling you off the last, and Mars-coloured Jupiter makes every interruption feel like a provocation. The body keeps score. A tight jaw, a short fuse by late afternoon, sleep that won't come because the engine's still running.

Whoever's closest tends to get it. A partner asks a simple question and gets the tone meant for your inbox. A flatmate finds the dishes done angrily. Kids, if you've got them, get the fast no. What helps is cutting the switching down. For one evening, do one thing and nothing else, whether that's cooking a meal start to finish with the phone in another room or fixing the hinge that's been loose for a month. If someone needs you in that hour, they can ring twice.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks in already moving, and with this card on the Ascendant people see someone with a lot on the go who seems to be enjoying it. Phone in one hand, coffee in the other, a quick hello and a good joke on the way past. The card lends your usual head-first entrance a lighter step. You come across as nimble, busy, hard to pin down and easy to like.

The square from Capricorn to Aries is where it rubs. Capricorn is the card's sign and it's the sign of the boss, the institution, the older person watching how you handle yourself. Those people see the speed and wonder whether it's control or luck. Jupiter borrows from Mars in Aries, having no standing of its own there, and that makes your approach to new things quick and a little greedy, grabbing the second opportunity before the first is properly in hand. From your side it feels like momentum. From theirs it can look like someone spreading themselves thin before they've been tested.

In a new job it's the person who volunteers for two committees in the first month. On a first date it's being great company and checking the time twice. With a landlord, a bank or anyone else deciding whether to trust you, it's the application sent from the car park with one field left blank. Pick the one first impression that matters most over the coming while and slow it right down. Arrive early, bring the paperwork, and let the other person finish talking.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on an Aries Ascendant, the card shows up as the rushed arrival. You come in late, flushed, apologising, with the last thing still on your mind, and people meet the scramble before they meet you. Or you overcorrect and come across as brusque, clipped, all business, because you've got four minutes and you want them to know it.

Interviews and first meetings suffer most. So do new neighbours, who decide from one hurried exchange in the hallway that you're a bit much. A new client gets your second-best attention because the best of it was on another call. Cut one thing out of the hour before anything that matters. Leave early, sit in the car or on a bench outside for five minutes, and walk in with only the one thing in your hands.

sun.upright:
Two coins, a figure keeping them both in motion, and ships riding a lot of water behind. For a Taurus Sun that's close to a nightmare and also, oddly, home ground. Capricorn trines Taurus. Both are earth, so this card speaks your language, the language of what's real, what's paid for, what you can hold in your hand. It's about money and material things in the plainest sense, and you know more about those than most people.

What it asks of you is movement, and that's the hard part. Taurus is fixed. You like the money where you put it, the plan the way it was agreed, the week to look like last week. Sharing an element with the card turns everything up, and that works both ways. You're very good at keeping things steady, and very good at refusing to shift a coin from one hand to the other even when the situation's plainly changed. Jupiter is a guest in Taurus with no rank there, taking its tone from Venus, so the growth on offer is comfortable growth, a bit more ease, a bit more pleasure, provided you let the money move.

With money this could be moving savings into something that actually earns, or evening out two incomes that arrive at different times. At work it's the steady job alongside the thing you make with your hands, and how much of each week each one gets. At home it might be reorganising who pays for what. Choose one sum that's been sitting still out of habit, look at where it could be doing more, and move it.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun with this card reversed tends to dig in. Something has changed, the rent, the hours, a partner's income, and you're still running the old budget as if it hadn't. Earth on earth makes the stubbornness solid. Or the Venus side takes over and comfort spending quietly borrows from the savings, a nice dinner here, a better chair there, until the careful balance you're proud of has a hole in it.

The bank account knows first, from the transfer you keep meaning to set up and the direct debit you've forgotten about. At work it's refusing the new system because the old one was fine. Sit down with the actual numbers from your statements for the last three months, and change one line of the budget to match what's really happening.

moon.upright:
Comfort for a Taurus Moon is the same thing, reliably, at the same time. The good bread, the familiar bed, money in the account where you left it. So when the Two of Pentacles turns up in the place of your feelings, something in your life is asking to be kept in motion, and your body will probably tell you about it before your head does.

The card is earth and so is your Moon, and Capricorn sits in trine to Taurus, so none of this is foreign. You feel money in your stomach. You feel a messy week in your shoulders. Jupiter, visiting Taurus with nothing special going for it, answers to Venus here, and that means the card's answer to stress is pleasure, a nice meal, a new jumper, something soft. Some of that is exactly right. Some of it is the balancing act done with a credit card. You'll know the low hum of unease when two parts of life won't settle into one routine, shift work next to a partner's nine to five, say.

In bed this is the half-hour awake doing sums. With food it's eating for comfort on the days the week gets away from you, and forgetting to eat on the others. A partner may notice you need one fixed thing, a meal together, a slow Sunday morning, that stays put while everything else moves. Pick that fixed thing, name it out loud, and guard it.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the card on a Taurus Moon usually means the routine has become the thing holding you up, and any change to it feels like the floor tilting. Two demands are competing and you're answering by clinging harder to the one habit you trust, the evening biscuit, the same takeaway, the long sleep-in, while the other demand gets quietly left on the step.

Money worry is common here, and it's less about the numbers than about feeling unsafe. Your body might show it as heaviness, a craving for sugar or salt, a reluctance to get off the couch that has nothing to do with being tired. A partner may find you immovable about small things. Choose one comfort you reach for automatically and swap it for a different one for a week, a walk instead of the snack, a bath instead of the scroll, so the soothing has to move a little.

rising.upright:
People meeting a Taurus Ascendant see someone calm, unhurried and hard to rattle. Put the Two of Pentacles on that and the impression becomes someone who can carry a lot without making a fuss about it, which is mostly true, and it's why you'll find people handing you things. The card is earth, your rising sign is earth, and Capricorn and Taurus sit in easy trine, so the look fits you like your own coat.

The risk is in the doubling up. When the card and the sign share an element you get more of the same, and the more capable and unbothered you look, the more gets put in your hands. Taurus rising doesn't like to be seen scrambling, so you keep the calm face on while you're privately moving three appointments around under the table. Jupiter holds no rank in Taurus and takes after Venus, and that gives the whole show a pleasant, easygoing finish. People think it's effortless. Nobody sees the spreadsheet on your phone.

At a new job this is being the steady pair of hands by the end of week two, and being given the budget, the roster and the office party. In the family it's the one everyone assumes can host. With new friends it's the person whose house becomes the default. Before you say yes to the next thing someone hands you, say 'let me check', and actually check.
rising.reversed:
When this card turns over for Taurus rising, the calm front starts to cost more than it gives. You look fine. You say you're fine. People keep handing you things because you look fine, and underneath the earth-on-earth steadiness you're stretched and a bit resentful. The other version is the immovable one, where you come across as slow or stubborn because you've quietly decided not to take on one more thing and haven't told anyone.

Colleagues are the first to misread it, either piling on or deciding you're difficult. Family hosting falls to you by default. New people get a polite, closed door. Say out loud, early, what you've got room for and what you haven't. Something like 'I can do Thursday but not the whole weekend' tells people where you are without a scene.

sun.upright:
On paper a Gemini Sun and a card about keeping two coins in the air should get on famously. You like having more than one of everything, and you'd like to be known as the one who can turn a hand to anything. This is a pentacle card, though. Pentacles are earth and Gemini is air, and those elements pull against each other, the idea against the invoice. So the card isn't only asking whether you can keep several things going. It's asking whether any of them is bringing anything in.

Jupiter, the planet behind the card, is in detriment in Gemini, the sign opposite its home, so it's working against the grain. It wants one big meaning and Gemini keeps breaking it into interesting pieces. Capricorn and Gemini are quincunx, which means they have nothing in common, and you'll feel that as a constant small adjusting between your curiosity and the card's demand for results. There is a foothold, though. Jupiter rules the first decan of Gemini, the Eight of Swords, the card of being hemmed in by your own thinking, and I've seen plenty of Gemini Suns talk themselves into a corner with options.

At work this is the freelance life, three clients and an invoice nobody's sent. In study it's the second course started before the first one's finished. With a brother or sister it might be the family business, or the family expectation, that you're balancing against your own thing. Write down what each project actually earned you last month, in money or in something you can name, and keep the two with the best answers.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the card finds a Gemini Sun with too many tabs open and a reputation for starting things. Jupiter in detriment gets scattered, growth spread so thin across so many ideas that none of them gets fed, and the Eight of Swords decan adds the feeling of being boxed in by choices you made yourself. Or it goes the other way. You get so worried about dropping something that you freeze and do none of it well.

People at work have probably started double-checking whether you'll deliver. The money is small amounts from lots of places and no clear picture of the total. A sibling might be waiting on a favour you promised and forgot. Close the projects you already know you won't finish. Tell the people involved, send the files back, and let the relief tell you which of the others to keep.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon settles. A good chat, a message back, something new to read, and the mood lifts. The card is a pentacle, earth through and through, and it doesn't settle through talk. It settles through doing, moving your weight from one foot to the other, and since air and earth are elements that work against each other, the card and your Moon calm down by different routes. You explain the stress, and the card wants you to handle it.

With Jupiter in detriment in your Moon's sign, working against the grain, the feeling side of things often gets too much input. Every article, every opinion, every voice note from a friend with a view on your situation. Jupiter wants the big reassuring answer and keeps finding forty small ones. The quincunx between Capricorn and Gemini has you making tiny adjustments all day, the reply rewritten, the plan shifted, and your nervous system notices even when you don't.

At bedtime this is the phone, one more thread, one more tab. Friends find you always available to talk and don't see you quietly running on empty. With a partner it's describing the problem beautifully and not asking for the practical help you actually need, a lift, a meal, a morning off. Try doing the sorting with your hands for once. Clear one drawer or one inbox to empty, and see whether the mood shifts before you've said a word about it.
moon.reversed:
The reversed card on a Gemini Moon is the jittery version. Your attention flicks between worries the way a thumb flicks between apps, and none of them gets resolved because you never stay with one long enough. The Eight of Swords, Jupiter's decan in your sign, is close by, and the feeling it brings is of being tied up in thoughts that aren't even that important.

Sleep usually goes first, a wired, chatty mind at one in the morning. Then friends get the same worry in three different versions. Your body might feel it as shallow breathing or a jiggling leg. Pick one worry, just the one, and do the first physical thing about it, the call, the form, the appointment. Leave the rest on a piece of paper by the kettle until you've done it.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising arrives talking, interested in everyone, apparently able to do six things at once. Drawn for your Ascendant, this card sharpens that into a very specific first impression, the capable multitasker, someone with a lot going on and a quick answer for all of it. People will assume you can handle the extra job, and they won't ask first.

What complicates it is that the card is earth and your rising sign is air. Those elements tug in opposite directions, which in practice means talk meeting proof. Strangers get the quick, clever version and go away impressed, and a few weeks later they're looking for the solid result that the first meeting implied. Jupiter's detriment in Gemini tends to show as a slightly overstretched manner, promising a bit more than you've thought through because it sounded right in the moment. The quincunx from Capricorn keeps the adjusting going. You're forever tweaking how you come across to fit whoever's in front of you.

At a networking event this is ten business cards and no follow-up. In a job interview it's the great answer about a skill you'd need to brush up on first. Dating, it's being fun on the first night and hard to schedule after. After your next first meeting, send one practical follow-up within a day, with a date or a document in it, so the impression has something solid under it.
rising.reversed:
Turned over on a Gemini Ascendant, the card makes you look double-booked, because you probably are. You turn up to the coffee still answering the last message, you get the time wrong, you apologise charmingly and people forgive you, the first time. Jupiter's detriment here spreads your attention so thin that each person gets a slice. The other risk is stage fright, the quick patter drying up because there are too many versions of you to choose from.

Over time this becomes a reputation at work for being lovely and hard to rely on. Friends start making plans that don't depend on you coming. In a new relationship it's the text answered six hours late with a very good excuse. Keep one calendar and put everything in it, including the things you think you'll remember. Then say no to the next invitation that clashes with anything already in there.

sun.upright:
Cancer and Capricorn face each other across the zodiac, so this card comes to a Cancer Sun from the far end of your own axis. Cancer is home, family, the people you feed. Capricorn is the job, the outside world, the standing you earn. The Two of Pentacles is almost a picture of that axis in motion, one coin for the house and one for the work, passed back and forth all week. For a sign that wants above all to provide and protect, it's familiar in a way that can make you tired just looking at it.

The good news sits with Jupiter. The card's planet is exalted in Cancer, an honoured guest at its most generous, so your version of this juggle has real warmth in it. You're not doing it for status. You're doing it so everyone's fed and the rent's paid and nobody has to worry, and that care is what keeps both coins moving. Water and earth get on well, too, so the card gives your feelings something practical to do. The strain is the opposition itself. Every hour you give to one end is an hour taken from the other, and a Cancer Sun keeps a very private tally of who missed out.

At work it's being the colleague who leaves at five on the dot and answers emails at ten. At home it's the family calendar on the fridge that only you understand. With a parent it can be helping them with money while keeping your own household afloat. Decide what enough looks like on each side, in hours, and write it on that calendar.
sun.reversed:
When this card is upside down for a Cancer Sun, the exalted Jupiter tips into over-giving. You're keeping everyone else's coins in the air and yours are rolling under the couch. The household runs, the kids or the parents or the partner are sorted, and your own work, the thing you were building for yourself, has been dropped so quietly that nobody noticed, including you for a while.

Money shows it as the family expense you absorbed without mentioning. The job shows it as the promotion you didn't go for because the hours wouldn't fit around everyone else. And home shows it as resentment that comes out sideways over something small. Pick one hour a week that belongs to your own work, put it where nobody can book over it, and don't explain why.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon needs a safe place to come back to. A kitchen that smells right, people who know your moods, a door you can close. This card doesn't sit still, and on the surface that's unsettling for a Moon in its own sign. Look closer and the astrology is kind to you here. Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, and earth gives water a shape to hold, so the Two brings a practical rhythm to your feelings, and a rhythm is a kind of safety you can carry around.

Capricorn is opposite Cancer, though, so the card still pulls from the other end. Part of you would like to stay home and look after everyone, and part of you has to go out and earn, organise, cope. You'll feel the swing in your body, the Sunday-evening dip before the week starts, the relief when you're back through your own front door. The card doesn't ask you to pick one. It asks you to find the rhythm between them so you aren't always missing one of them.

With family this is the phone call to your mother slotted between meetings. With food it's cooking a big batch on the weekend so the weekdays hold. Sleep wants a bedtime that stays the same whatever else moves. Choose one small ritual that happens in both places, a particular tea at your desk and at home, say, and let it tell your body that both are yours.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Cancer Moon, the card often means you're worrying about providing. Money, food in the house, whether everyone's all right, and the worry runs on a loop because Cancer is cardinal water and keeps starting the same wave. Jupiter's exaltation turned inside out becomes catastrophising, a generous imagination picturing every way it could go wrong. Some nights it isn't even your worry, it's a parent's or a child's, carried for them.

Three in the morning is when it's loudest. It's also in the fridge you keep overstocking, and in the partner you keep checking on. Your stomach may be where you feel it first. What helps is making the worry concrete. Write the actual figures, what's coming in and what's going out, on one page, and look at it in daylight with a cup of tea, somewhere other than your bed.

rising.upright:
Strangers meeting Cancer rising usually pick up care first. You notice who hasn't got a drink, you remember the name of someone's dog, you come across as protective and a little guarded. Draw this card for your mask and the impression people get is of someone holding a household together while also turning up to everything else. The parent with the laptop at the school gate, whether or not you have children. The friend who brought a casserole and left early for a shift.

Jupiter's exaltation in Cancer means the card lands kindly on your front door and makes the juggle look warm and capable. Capricorn sits opposite your rising sign, which puts it on your Descendant, the point where you meet other people one to one. So the card's sign is what you're facing across the table. Partners and colleagues tend to bring you the Capricorn side, the structure, the deadlines, the ambition, and you meet it with your Cancer side, and the pull between them keeps you moving. Your shell helps. People rarely see the strain.

In a new job this reads as dependable, the one who covers when someone's kid is sick. In friendships it's being the host and the helper and the one who remembers birthdays. With a partner it can mean doing the emotional admin while they do the career admin. Let someone see you drop one coin, just once, in a small way, and watch how they respond.
rising.reversed:
For Cancer rising, the card reversed tends to show on your face. You come in harried, apologising for the mess in the car, half your mind on who's picking up whom, and the shell goes up hard because you don't want anyone seeing how close to the edge the week is. The exalted Jupiter has already given most of its generosity away before you've walked through the door. People read what's left as prickly or distant.

New colleagues may decide you're not a team player when really you're leaving at three for a very good reason you haven't explained. A new friend gets cancelled on twice. A date gets the guarded version. Tell people a little of the real situation early, one plain sentence about what you're carrying at home, and give them the chance to adjust around it.

sun.upright:
The figure on this card is performing a little. Tall hat, one foot kicked up, keeping the coins moving as if there's a crowd watching, and a Leo Sun will recognise the instinct. You want to do things well and you want it seen, ideally without anyone guessing how hard it was. Capricorn and Leo are quincunx, five signs apart and sharing nothing, so this card's patient, practical kind of juggling and your wish to shine keep needing small corrections to sit together.

Jupiter has no special standing in Leo and takes its colour from the Sun, your own ruler, so in your chart the card's appetite turns warm, generous and slightly theatrical. You'll want the job and the creative thing, the family and the big plan, and you'll want to be good at all of it in front of people. The card also has a foothold in your sign. Jupiter rules the middle ten degrees of Leo, the decan of the Six of Wands, which is the card of the parade and the laurel wreath. So for you the balancing act gets tangled up with recognition. Some of the load is there because it's needed, and some of it, to be honest, because being the one who handles everything is a part you enjoy playing.

At work it looks like leading the visible project while keeping the dull admin going underneath, and minding that nobody thanks you for the admin. Money-wise it's being generous with friends while your own savings sit untouched. With a child, or a creative project, it's finding hours you don't really have. Tell one person which part of the load you carry unseen, and ask them to take a piece of it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down for a Leo Sun, the show can outlast the energy behind it. You keep smiling, you keep saying it's all under control, and the coins go round faster because stopping would mean admitting you took on too much. Pride does a lot of the damage with this card reversed. The Sun-coloured Jupiter hates to look ordinary, so you'd sooner drop something privately, the gym, the call to your dad, a decent night's sleep, than be seen dropping anything in public.

Health tends to pay first, in late nights and the energy crash that arrives on a Sunday afternoon. A partner notices you're brilliant at parties and short with them at home. The creative thing you love gets pushed back to after this busy patch, which never quite ends. Pick the public commitment you'd be most embarrassed to give up and give it up anyway, or at least halve it. Most people won't think any less of you, and a few will be relieved.

moon.upright:
Feelings in a Leo Moon run warm and want someone paying proper attention. You're soothed by being noticed and loved out loud, and you sulk a bit when you're not, which you probably know. This card brings a busier kind of emotional weather. Several people need you at once, or two parts of your life want your heart at the same time, and nobody claps for keeping it all going.

Leo is fixed fire and the card is earth, and those two elements have no quarrel and no particular bond, so the steady, practical coping this card is good at doesn't come to you by instinct. You have to go and get it. Jupiter, just visiting Leo, borrows the Sun's warmth, which makes your needs big-hearted. You want everyone happy and you'd like to be the reason. The quincunx between Capricorn and your Moon sign feels like a low-level mismatch. What would actually calm you, a list, a routine, a sensible early night, seems a bit beneath you, and what you're craving, a grand gesture from someone, doesn't fix the week.

With a partner it's wanting a proper evening together and finding it's the only free slot for the laundry. With friends it's being the life of the group chat while privately feeling unseen. The body shows it in your energy, bright in the morning and flat by four. Plan one evening that's purely for fun and put it in the diary with the same seriousness you'd give the dentist.
moon.reversed:
Hurt pride tends to run things when this card turns over on a Leo Moon. You've been carrying a lot and nobody's said thank you, so you start keeping score, and it comes out as a dramatic outburst over something small or a wounded, dignified silence that lasts two days. The other version is giving extravagantly to feel loved, gifts and favours and yes to everything, until there's nothing left in the tank for you.

Home is where it lands most, with a partner or a child getting the mood that really belongs to the week. Friends may get a flurry of plans followed by nothing. Sleep can go when you lie there replaying who didn't notice what. Tell the person closest to you, in plain words, that you could do with some appreciation, and when it comes, let them give it without brushing it off.

rising.upright:
Leo rising comes into a room as if it's an entrance, and with this card on the Ascendant the entrance has props. A bag over each shoulder, two conversations going, a story about your morning that has everyone laughing before you've sat down. People read you as someone who carries a lot and does it with style. That's mostly accurate, and it's a flattering way to be seen.

Capricorn, the sign behind the card, is quincunx to Leo, which is an awkward angle to work with. Capricorn wants the effort to look sensible and earned. Leo wants it to look easy and a little glamorous. You'll feel yourself fiddling between the two, dressing down for the meeting and then putting the good earrings back in, playing down how busy you are and then telling the whole story anyway. Jupiter holds no rank in Leo and follows the Sun's lead, so your first impression is big and generous and people warm to you fast. Under that sits the Six of Wands, the decan Jupiter rules in the middle of your sign, and a lot of people with Leo rising do quietly expect a bit of a welcome when they arrive.

Starting a new job, this is being handed the visible task in the first week and learning the boring systems in your own time. On a date it's being fantastic company and a little hard to read underneath. With neighbours or other parents it's being the person everyone assumes will run the fundraiser. Let one new person see you do something ordinary, like forgetting their name and asking again.
rising.reversed:
Turned upside down for Leo rising, the card makes the show harder to keep up. You still arrive with the big smile and the good story, but you're late, or double-booked, or the story is covering for the fact that the thing isn't done. Sometimes it goes the other way and you come across as flat and a bit grand at the same time, holding your warmth back because you're tired and don't want anyone to see.

It shows mostly at work, as the presentation you winged, and in the first weeks anywhere new, when people haven't seen your good side yet and catch you stretched. Friends may find you charming and not really there. A new partner could take the distraction personally. Before the next meeting that matters, cut what you're bringing down to one thing and prepare it properly, even if that means cancelling something else to find the time.

sun.upright:
Keeping two coins going is more or less a Virgo Sun's ordinary week. The job and the upkeep, the work and the endless small maintenance that keeps a life running, and you want to be useful at all of it and to get it right. Capricorn and Virgo are both earth and sit in trine, so the card speaks your language fluently. That shared element turns everything up, the competence and the fuss, in roughly equal amounts.

Jupiter is in detriment in Virgo, placed in the sign opposite its home, and it has to work against the grain here. Jupiter likes the big picture and the generous estimate. Virgo likes the detail and the exact figure. So the card's looseness, the knack of letting things wobble and trusting them to come right, is the bit you'll struggle with. I've seen a lot of Virgo Suns keep both coins going beautifully and then lie awake over the fact that one of them went slightly off course at half past two. Virgo is mutable, so you can adapt perfectly well. You'd just prefer to adapt to a plan you wrote yourself.

At work you're the person holding the systems together and fixing other people's mistakes before anyone sees them. With your health it's the routine you keep faithfully until one busy fortnight breaks it and you decide you've failed. With money it's the budget tracked to the cent. Choose one area where good enough really is good enough, the house or the inbox, and leave it at eighty per cent on purpose.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun under this card reversed can get very busy being busy. The Jupiter detriment shows as a habit of taking on more and more small jobs, each one reasonable on its own, until there's no room left for your own work and you're doing everyone else's tidying up. Or perfectionism freezes the whole juggle. You won't start the second thing until the first is flawless, so neither moves.

At work people may be leaning on you for the fiddly tasks while someone else gets the interesting ones. Your body might carry it as a nervous stomach or shoulders up round your ears. At home it can turn into a running commentary on how others fold the towels. Write down every task you've picked up that nobody actually asked you to do, and stop doing the three you mind most.

moon.upright:
The sea behind the figure is rough and the ships are riding it, and a Virgo Moon mostly feels safe when things are sorted, labelled and put back where they go. So the card's cheerful comfort with motion is a stretch for you. You settle yourself by fixing things. When a feeling gets too big you clean the bathroom, and it works, up to a point.

Your Moon shares the card's element, earth, and the trine between Capricorn and Virgo lets them understand each other without effort. The card offers you something your Moon already knows, that looking after practical things is a way of looking after yourself. Doubling the element doubles the worry too, though. Jupiter is in detriment in Virgo, so its reassurance struggles to reach you. You might have enough money, enough time and a partner who loves you, and still feel that one loose thread will bring the lot down. Your gut tends to pick that up before your head admits it.

With food it's the same careful lunch every day, and feeling off when the routine breaks. At night it's the list running through your head. With a friend or a partner it's showing love by doing things for them, and not quite letting them do things for you. Hand someone else one of your jobs for a fortnight, the shopping or the bins, and don't check how they're doing it.
moon.reversed:
Worry gets physical for a Virgo Moon when this card is reversed. You're doing a dozen small things to keep everything in order, none of them brings relief, so you do another dozen. The Jupiter detriment can make every gap look enormous. One missed payment feels like ruin. One short reply from a friend feels like the end of the friendship.

Sleep and digestion are the usual places it settles, and you know your own signals well. At work it can look like reading an email four times before you send it. With a partner it's snapping at them for loading the dishwasher wrong. A plain physical routine helps you here, often better than thinking it through. Walk the same route each morning for a week, same time, no podcast, and let your legs do the work while your mind does its sorting.

rising.upright:
The person who notices the typo on the menu and doesn't mention it is very often Virgo rising. You meet the world as competent, observant and a bit reserved, and with the Two of Pentacles on that doorway you come across as the capable one, organised and useful, handling a lot without fuss. People hand you their spreadsheets and their spare keys quite early on.

An earth card on an earth Ascendant, with Capricorn and Virgo in trine, makes you look very together. The catch is Jupiter's detriment in your rising sign. The card's easygoing, generous side has to push against Virgo's habit of reviewing everything, and strangers sometimes see the effort. You can seem tense when you're only paying attention. Virgo is mutable as well, so your instinct is to adapt to whoever's in front of you, adjusting your pace and your manner, and the card doubles that. You can walk into almost any situation and quietly work out what's needed. It's a real skill. It's also how you end up doing the washing up at someone else's party.

In your first month somewhere new this is being given the messy project because you seemed sensible. With new friends it's being the one who books the table and works out who owes what. In dating, people can read your care as caution. Next time you meet someone new, let them watch you laugh at a small mistake of yours before you've fixed it.
rising.reversed:
Flipped on a Virgo Ascendant, the card makes you look harried, which is the last thing you want. You arrive with a notebook and a worried face, apologising for something nobody noticed, or you seem fussy because you're trying to keep six small things straight in your head at once. The Jupiter detriment tips into over-preparing, so every first meeting feels like an exam you might fail.

New workplaces may peg you as the admin person, which isn't what you're there for. Dates can find you hard to relax around. Neighbours might only ever see you rushing out with your keys in your teeth. Arrive at the next new thing with less, no notes, no backup plan, just the one question you actually want answered, and let people meet the plainer version of you.

sun.upright:
Libra likes a balance, and this card is a picture of one, so a Libra Sun might assume it's on home ground. It's a different kind of balance, though. Libra weighs things and wants them level, the scales at rest and everyone treated fairly. The Two of Pentacles never gets anything level. It keeps things moving, and it's interested in what gets paid and what gets done. Capricorn squares Libra. Both are cardinal signs, both want to be the one starting things, and the square between them is friction that pushes you to act.

Jupiter holds no dignity in Libra and takes after Venus, your ruler, so the card's appetite comes out as a wish to please. You say yes to the extra role because saying no would feel rude. Earth, the card's element, sits awkwardly with your air, idea against proof, and that's where you'll feel it most. You can talk beautifully about how you'll fit it all in, and then the actual week happens. There's a small foothold here too. Jupiter rules the last ten degrees of Libra, the decan of the Four of Swords, the card of rest and recovery, so if your Sun sits late in the sign, part of what this card is teaching you is when to stop.

In a partnership it's keeping two sets of needs going, yours and theirs, and usually giving theirs the better deal. At work it can be keeping the peace between two colleagues while doing your own job on the side. Money means the joint account and the private one. Make one decision on your own, about your own time, without asking anyone what they think.
sun.reversed:
For a Libra Sun the reversed card usually means you've agreed to too much so as not to let anyone down. The Venus-flavoured Jupiter makes every request sound reasonable, and the square from Capricorn turns the pile into pressure that you mostly feel as guilt. Or you swing the other way and can't choose at all, so both coins hang in the air and nothing moves.

Relationships are usually where it shows, as resentment you're too polite to mention or plans made around everyone except you. At work it's the task you took on to keep someone happy and are now doing badly. The Four of Swords sits in the last part of your sign, and rest is often the real fix. Take one full evening with no plans and no messages, and tell people beforehand so you don't feel you owe anyone an explanation afterwards.

moon.upright:
An argument in the house sits in a Libra Moon's chest until it's resolved, even when it isn't your argument. You feel settled when the people around you are getting on, and you'll work quite hard, often without noticing, to make sure they are. This card turns up with a lot of competing needs, and your reflex will be to balance everyone else's before your own, as if keeping the peace were one of the coins.

What the card offers and what you reach for come from elements that pull apart, earth and air. You process by talking it through, weighing it up, getting a second opinion. The card would like you to just handle it, one thing and then the next. Capricorn squares Libra, cardinal against cardinal, and the feeling of that square is a push to act before you've finished considering. Jupiter, a guest in your Moon's sign without any standing of its own, follows Venus, so your comfort comes from pleasant things and pleasant people. A tidy room calms you. So does a friend who agrees with you.

With a partner it shows as a quiet tally of whether things are fair, who did the school run, who cooked, and unease when it's lopsided. With friends it's being everyone's sounding board. In the body it can be shallow breathing and a stiff neck whenever there's tension in the room. The next time someone asks what you'd like, give them the honest answer, even if it tips things out of balance for an evening.
moon.reversed:
A Libra Moon tends to go very quiet about what it needs under this card reversed. You're so busy smoothing things over, the partner's mood, the friend's crisis, the family group chat, that your own feelings get parked and then forgotten about. The friction between earth and air makes it worse, because you know what you ought to do and can't make yourself do it.

Close relationships take the strain, often as a sudden flash of resentment over something tiny. Sleep can turn restless. You might find yourself shopping or rearranging the furniture to feel better, which works for about a day. Pick one thing you've been going along with that you don't actually like, the music in the car, the standing Sunday lunch, the way a friend talks to you, and say so kindly, once.

rising.upright:
People meeting Libra rising see charm first. You're easy to talk to, you dress well for the occasion, you leave the other person feeling the meeting went well. This card on your Ascendant adds the look of someone graceful under a heavy load, smiling and relaxed and plainly doing several things while making it look nice.

The square from Capricorn shows in how you start things. Both signs are cardinal and both like to set things going, but Capricorn's way is serious and results-first where yours is social and collaborative. You'll notice it in meetings where you'd like to warm the room up first and someone else wants the agenda done in ten minutes. Because this is an earth card on an air sign, strangers sometimes wonder, after a pleasant first half-hour, whether there's substance under the charm, and you'll need to show them something concrete. Jupiter has no standing in Libra and follows Venus, which makes your approach generous and diplomatic, occasionally to a fault.

In a job interview it's getting on famously with the panel and then being asked for figures. In a new friendship it's remembering everyone's birthday and forgetting your own plans. On a date you're lovely company, and you ask so much about the other person that they go home knowing nothing about you. When you next meet someone who matters, bring one piece of real evidence, a number or a finished piece of work, and put it on the table early.
rising.reversed:
Indecision in public is how this card reversed tends to look on Libra rising. You arrive having not quite settled on the outfit, the restaurant, or which of two invitations to accept, and people read it as vagueness. Or the charm wears thin, a practised smile over obvious tiredness, and the square to Capricorn makes you look as if you're going through the motions.

First meetings at work suffer, where you're pleasant and hard to pin down. Dates may find you so agreeable that you never say anything real. Friends get double-booked and find out on the night. Before your next social thing, decide in advance what you'll do if two requests clash, and stick to it when it comes up, whoever's asking.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't usually do light. You go all in, you want to know what's underneath, and your purpose tends to be one thing held very tightly. A card about a figure skipping about on a beach with two coins can look like a strange match for you. The astrology says otherwise. Capricorn sits sextile to Scorpio, two signs apart, a friendly angle that opens a door you still have to use. And your water and the card's earth get on well, the earth giving the water somewhere to go.

Jupiter has no particular standing in Scorpio and borrows from Mars, the sign's traditional ruler, so the card's appetite turns strategic. You're not juggling to look busy. You've got two coins going because you've worked out you need both, the steady income and the thing you're really building, or the public role and the private project nobody knows about yet. It feels like being in control, and you like that. The part that asks something new of you is the looseness. You're probably holding on tighter than you need to.

In money terms this is keeping a second stream quiet and steady until it's ready. At work it can be doing the job well while quietly getting ready to leave it. With a partner it's deciding how much of the plan to share. Pick the person you trust most and tell them what the second coin is for.
sun.reversed:
Secrecy is what this card reversed usually looks like for a Scorpio Sun, and by this stage the secret has become a weight. You're keeping a balance nobody else knows about, a debt, a second job, a decision you've half made, and keeping it hidden is costing you as much as the thing itself. Jupiter takes on Mars's edge in your sign, and that can make you stubborn about a strategy that plainly isn't working, because changing course would feel like losing.

Money is the likeliest place for it, especially shared money you haven't been straight about. Work comes next, where you're doing two jobs' worth and resenting it silently. A partner may sense something's being kept from them and start digging. Tell one person the whole of it, the actual numbers or the actual plan, and let them help you decide which coin to put down.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel things deeply and privately, and what makes you safe is knowing exactly where you stand, with people and with money. You need to trust before you relax, and you'd sooner feel everything than feel a little. This card comes into that intensity with its constant rebalancing, and part of you will find it exhausting while another part is secretly relieved.

The relief comes from the elements. Water and earth are on good terms, each giving the other shape, so the card's practical side gives your feelings somewhere solid to land. When you're churned up, handling actual things helps, paying the bill, clearing out the cupboard, taking the car in. The sextile from Capricorn opens that option without forcing it on you. Jupiter, a visitor here that takes its lead from Mars, makes your emotional needs strong and a bit all-or-nothing. You'd like to know which feeling is the true one. The card's view is that both can be true for a while, and you can keep them moving until it's clearer.

With a partner this is loving them and feeling wary at the same time, and not needing to settle it straight away. With money it's the private safety net you keep and check on a lot. Sleep runs deep and heavy when things are good and very light when they aren't. Next time you're churning, do a physical job with a clear end, and only decide how you feel once it's finished.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Scorpio Moon, the balancing turns into brooding. Something's out of kilter, a friendship, a bank balance, a suspicion about a partner, and instead of shifting your weight you go very still and very watchful. Jupiter picks up Mars's heat in your sign, and that can turn the brooding into a plan for getting even, which you won't act on, mostly, but it eats up the evenings.

It often sits in the body as a tight jaw or an aching lower back, and in sleep that's light and full of dreams. Shared money becomes a sore point. Someone close may feel shut out without knowing why. Get the worry out of your head and onto paper, then bin the paper, and do something with your hands afterwards, cooking or weeding, anything that ends in a result you can see.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives off a certain intensity even when you're only ordering a coffee. People sense you're watching, that you've clocked more than you're saying, and they're a bit careful around you at first. With this card drawn for your mask, what they pick up is someone with a lot going on who is absolutely not going to tell them what.

The sextile from Capricorn makes that a workable combination. It's an easy angle, but it only pays off if you use it, and here using it means letting people see some of your practical side. Earth sits comfortably with your water, so you come across as grounded as well as deep, and people tend to trust you with serious things. Jupiter holds nothing special in Scorpio and borrows from Mars, so your instinct in any new situation is to size it up, work out the angles, then commit completely. You adapt quietly. You'll change your whole approach halfway through a meeting and nobody will see you do it.

Walking into a new workplace, you read as capable and a bit mysterious, and people will wonder what else you do. On a first date you're magnetic and give away very little. With anyone who handles your money, a bank, an accountant, a landlord, you come across as someone who knows exactly what they're doing. Give one new person one real detail about what you're juggling, and notice how much warmer they get.
rising.reversed:
When the card is upside down on Scorpio rising, the mystery hardens into a wall. You come across as guarded and hard to read, which you are, because you're stretched and don't want anyone to see it. Or the Mars side of Jupiter makes you intense in a way that puts people off, too much focus on one point in a conversation that needed a lighter touch.

At work, colleagues might decide you're cold when you're really managing a crisis at home. New friendships stall because you don't give enough away. People you're negotiating with might read the tiredness as hostility. Before a first meeting that matters, choose one small, true thing about yourself that you're happy to share, and share it in the first ten minutes.

sun.upright:
Jupiter is your planet. It rules Sagittarius and it's at home there, and this card is Jupiter working in Capricorn, so the Two of Pentacles comes to a Sagittarius Sun with your own ruler's signature on it. It knows how you think. You want more, bigger, further, and you're usually confident it'll all work out, which it often does.

What the card brings is the side of Jupiter that's had to learn some manners. In Capricorn it's in fall, cramped and made to prove itself, and it has to find a roundabout way to do its job. Capricorn and Sagittarius sit side by side in the zodiac, a semi-sextile, and neighbours like that have little in common and each has what the other lacks. Capricorn has patience and a budget. You have faith and a plane ticket. So the card is your ruler showing you what its big appetite looks like when it has to live inside limits, and that's useful and a bit irritating, to be honest. Mutable fire loves taking on one more thing. The card's earth won't fight your fire, but it won't warm to it either, so the steadiness has to be asked in.

With money it's the trip and the rent in the same month, and actually covering both. At work it's the teaching or selling or travelling alongside the admin nobody enjoys. In study it's the course you've started while working full time. Before you add the next exciting thing, write down what it'll cost in hours a week, and see whether the number still excites you.
sun.reversed:
A Sagittarius Sun with this card reversed usually has too many adventures on the go and not enough ground under them. Jupiter at home in your sign is generous and overconfident, and without Capricorn's brakes it says yes to the trip, the course, the new venture and a friend's project, all in the same breath. Something drops, and it's usually the dull thing, the tax return or the phone bill.

Check money first, then your promises, the ones made cheerfully that you can't keep any more. A partner may feel they come second to your plans. Your energy may run high for a fortnight and then collapse into a weekend on the couch. Go through everything you've committed to and, for each one, ask whether you'd say yes again if it were offered to you fresh.

moon.upright:
Room to move is what settles a Sagittarius Moon. A road, a plan, a new idea, something good to look forward to. You get restless when life closes in, and a bit gloomy if there's nothing on the horizon. This card brings motion, which you like, and responsibility, which you like less, and it hands you both at once.

Jupiter rules your Moon sign and this is Jupiter's card, so emotionally it speaks with real authority. It's your own ruler reporting back from a harder posting, Capricorn, where it's in fall and has to work within limits. You'll feel that as a restless optimism that keeps bumping into practical facts, the budget, the diary, somebody else's needs. The semi-sextile between Capricorn and Sagittarius means the two signs don't naturally understand each other, though each has what the other is short of. Your need for freedom and the card's need for order can actually help each other out, if you let them. Earth and fire need to be introduced, and in your feelings the introduction usually happens after a bit of grumbling.

Sleep may be patchy when you're excited about something and can't settle. With a partner it's needing both the adventure and the steady home, and swinging between them. In the body, energy comes in bursts and you tend to overdo it. Plan something to look forward to that you can genuinely afford, a day trip somewhere you've never been, and book it.
moon.reversed:
Obligations start to feel like a cage for a Sagittarius Moon when this card turns over. You wanted freedom and you've got a rota. The restlessness comes out as irritability, or as escape, the late-night browsing of flights, the new plan hatched at midnight that has nothing to do with the problem in front of you.

Home is where it bites, with a partner or family asking for reliability you don't feel like giving. Friends may get the sulky version of you, the one who says it's fine when it clearly isn't. Money can turn into a way to feel free and then into a source of stress. Your body may feel twitchy and underused. What helps is movement with a practical edge. Walk somewhere you genuinely need to go, the shops or work, instead of driving, and let the walk be the adventure for the day.

rising.upright:
People tend to like Sagittarius rising within about a minute. You meet the world with an open, friendly energy, a big laugh and an obvious appetite for whatever's next. Draw the Two of Pentacles for this Ascendant and people see an adventurer who is also, surprisingly, on top of things. Travel plans and a job. A side business and a family. You seem to have been given extra hours that nobody else got.

Jupiter is your chart ruler, since it rules your rising sign, and this card is Jupiter working in Capricorn, so it's a direct line to how you start things. It's the version of your ruler that's been made to do the accounts. Jupiter is in fall in Capricorn, and on your manner that shows as a touch of caution under the charm, as if you've learned from the last time you overcommitted. With the signs only semi-sextile, the two approaches don't blend easily. You'll catch yourself agreeing to something with your usual enthusiasm and then, a second later, doing the maths. Fire and earth need introducing to each other, and you end up being the one who does it.

Offered a new role, you're the one who volunteers for the overseas project and somehow also gets asked to fix the budget. With new friends it's organising the trip and keeping track of who paid. On a date it's great stories and a slight hesitation about a second one until you've checked the diary. Next time you're offered something exciting, ask one practical question before you say yes.
rising.reversed:
On a Sagittarius Ascendant, the reversed card often reads as overpromising. You arrive full of enthusiasm and plans, people take you at your word, and a month later the plans have fallen through because there were too many of them. Or you seem scattered and restless, always halfway out of the door, too keen on the next thing to be present for this one.

New colleagues tend to see it first, as someone brilliant who doesn't follow through. New partners get a thrilling start and then patchy contact. Friends start treating your invitations as maybes. A landlord or a bank may want a steadier picture than the one you're giving them. Say yes to fewer things in the first weeks of anything new, and finish each one before you mention the next.

sun.upright:
This is one of your own sign's cards. The Two of Pentacles belongs to the first ten degrees of Capricorn, the slice of the sign Jupiter rules, so a Capricorn Sun is getting a card that comes from home, and if your Sun sits in those early degrees it's closer still. It's about managing, building, carrying responsibility and keeping it all going, which is roughly what you'd like to be known for.

Jupiter is in fall in Capricorn, uncomfortable and not properly heard, and it has to find an indirect way to get its work done. That's the interesting part for you. Jupiter wants to grow and be generous, and your sign wants to be careful, measured and sure of the ground. So the card describes growth earned a step at a time, often through the back door, with Saturn, your ruler, checking every step. Being the same element turns all of it up. You're very good at this, and you're very good at overdoing it, taking on a second responsibility because nobody else will and telling yourself you'll rest once it's done. I've seen Capricorn Suns say that for about fifteen years.

At work this is the promotion that comes with twice the admin, and managing it anyway. With money it's careful growth, the extra repayment, the investment you researched for months. With a parent it may be taking on their affairs alongside your own. Let yourself enjoy one thing that's going well, out loud and with someone, before you move on to fixing the next thing.
sun.reversed:
For a Capricorn Sun this card reversed is often the workhorse problem. You've been carrying two jobs' worth of responsibility, and Jupiter's fall in your sign means there's no generosity left over for yourself. No treats, no days off, no sense of how far you've come. Or the ambition has stalled, both coins stuck in the air, and you're grimly waiting for conditions to improve.

Work usually shows it first, in the long hours or the plan that's been on hold for a year. Your body might hold it as stiffness in the back and shoulders. A partner or a friend may tell you you're never fully off. Pick one responsibility that isn't really yours, the committee, the family admin, a colleague's slack, and hand it back to whoever it belongs to.

moon.upright:
Safety for a Capricorn Moon usually means having the practical side under control. Enough in the bank, the plan in place, a sense that it's handled so you don't have to feel too much about it. This card is one of Capricorn's own, the card of its first decan, so emotionally it's talking in your mother tongue. It's about coping, and you know how to cope.

The trouble is that sharing an element means the card amplifies whatever's already there. Your steadiness gets steadier, and so does your habit of dealing with feelings by writing a list. Jupiter's fall in your sign is the emotional heart of this. Jupiter brings comfort and faith and a sense that things will be fine, and in Capricorn it struggles to get a word in. You may find it hard to let yourself feel hopeful, as if hope were a risk you can't afford. So you keep both coins going, the work and the worry, and you don't notice you're tired until you're very tired.

Sleep may be the first thing to go, especially the early waking with a head full of tasks. In the family you're probably the one everyone relies on and nobody checks on. At work you feel calmer the more responsibility you're given, which is great until it isn't. Let one person look after you in a practical way, cook for you or drive you somewhere, and don't pay them back straight away.
moon.reversed:
The reversed card on a Capricorn Moon usually means the coping has turned into grinding. You're managing everything, it's all under control on paper, and there's a flatness to your days, a sense that nothing's enjoyable because everything's a task. Jupiter's fall makes it hard to find the lift, the thing that would make the effort feel worthwhile.

It tends to show in the body first, as stiffness, headaches, meals eaten standing at the bench. Your partner may notice you've stopped laughing at things. Money worry can run high even when the figures are fine. Plan one small, completely unproductive pleasure a week, a film in the afternoon, a long swim, a walk with nowhere to get to, and do it without justifying it to yourself.

rising.upright:
Strangers trust Capricorn rising on sight to be competent. You come across as serious and capable, older than your years when you're young and younger than them later on. With this card on your Ascendant, that impression widens into someone carrying a lot of responsibility with a lightness that surprises people. There's a dry humour in it too, and they catch it.

The card comes from your own rising sign, the first decan of Capricorn, and it's earth on earth, so it fits your manner neatly and turns it up. Saturn rules Capricorn, which makes it your chart ruler, and Saturn likes things done properly and in order. Jupiter is in fall here, and in how you meet the world that shows as holding your enthusiasm back. You're keener on new things than you let on. You'll approach a new job or a new person carefully, weigh up what you're taking on, and then take it all on anyway, because you can.

At work this reads as the safe pair of hands, and you'll be given responsibility faster than you asked for it. In a new friendship it's being the organised one, the host, the one with the spare charger. In dating, people may take a while to find out how funny you are. Let the first impression run a bit looser than usual next time, and tell the joke or the story you'd normally save for the third meeting.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising with this card reversed tends to come across as overburdened and closed. You're polite and efficient, people can see you're carrying too much, and it makes them either pile more on or keep their distance. The earth-on-earth doubling can make you look rigid, when often it's just tiredness.

It shows in new jobs especially, when you take on responsibility too fast and look strained by the end of the first month. First dates can feel like interviews. Neighbours might only see the person rushing to the car with a coffee. Before the next first meeting, put down one thing you're carrying, a task handed over, a worry parked for the day, so you arrive with less on your shoulders and your face shows it.

sun.upright:
An Aquarius Sun usually wants to do something that matters beyond itself, a cause, a group, an idea about how things could work better. You like being the one who thinks differently. This card brings the practical side of all that. Keeping the lights on while you change the world. A day job and a passion project, or a community role and a family.

Jupiter has no dignity in Aquarius and takes its colour from Saturn, your traditional ruler, which gives the card's growth a disciplined, slightly austere feel in your chart. You'll expand, but on your own terms and inside a structure you've thought through. The friction to name is between the card's earth and your air. You can see exactly how it should work, and the card asks you to show it working. Capricorn and Aquarius are neighbours, a semi-sextile with little in common, though Capricorn can lend you the follow-through your plans are sometimes missing. Aquarius is fixed, too, so once you've decided how to do something you don't love adjusting, which is awkward with a card that's all adjustment.

With a group or a cause this is the unpaid organising alongside the paid work. With money it's funding your principles, the ethical bank, the donation, the lower-paid job you believe in. With friends it's being there for everyone and a little distant from each one. Choose one idea you've been talking about for ages and give it a budget, in hours and money, on paper.
sun.reversed:
The gap between the vision and the logistics is where an Aquarius Sun feels this card reversed. You've taken on the cause and the job and a friend's crisis, and the Saturn tone of Jupiter makes you grimly determined not to drop any of them, even though the energy's gone. Or you detach, going cool and theoretical while the practical tasks pile up around you.

Groups are often where it shows, as the committee you're holding up alone. Money comes next, where your principles and the rent disagree. Close friends may find you hard to reach, and you may find yourself answering group emails at midnight. Hand one of your causes to someone else for a while, properly, with a handover, and let yourself be an ordinary member of something for once.

moon.upright:
Emotionally, Aquarius Moons like a bit of space. You feel things fully, but you'd like to think them through at arm's length, and you're most at ease with friends who don't need constant reassurance. This card brings the tug of many needs at once, and your first instinct is to manage them with your head, making a plan, seeing the system.

Your Moon's air and the card's earth don't meet easily. The card is physical and practical. It calms things by handling them. You calm things by understanding them, and the two can work together, but only if you let your hands do some of the work. Jupiter, a guest in Aquarius, takes its colour from Saturn, so the comfort the card offers is sober. A well-organised week, a savings buffer, a bedtime. It isn't glamorous, and it helps. Capricorn and Aquarius sit side by side without much in common, and yet the card can give your Moon the ground it sometimes lacks.

With friends, it's being the one everyone brings their problems to, and holding it all very calmly. With a partner it's needing closeness and also a door you can shut. The body may run on nervous energy, with sleep drifting later and later. Build one physical anchor into each day, a set bedtime or a walk after lunch, and keep it even when the day is chaotic.
moon.reversed:
Detachment is the usual way an Aquarius Moon copes with this card reversed. You go cool and efficient, answer everything calmly and feel very little, because feeling it would slow you down. The Saturn tone Jupiter takes on in your sign can make it bleak, a sense of duty with no warmth left in it. Underneath, you're usually carrying a good share of other people's worries, and it's easier to organise them than to feel them.

Friends often notice first, since you're present in the group chat and absent in person. A partner may feel shut out. At work you might be the calmest person in the room and the most tired. Sleep can go odd, too late or too broken. Pick one friend and do something physical together, a walk, a swim, cooking a meal, and let the conversation go wherever it goes.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising tends to come across as friendly and slightly unusual, the one with the interesting job or the unexpected opinion. With this card on the Ascendant, people meet someone who seems to be running several things at once in their own way, with their own system, and doing it with a cheerful sort of independence.

Saturn is your traditional chart ruler, since it rules Aquarius, and the card's Jupiter takes its tone from Saturn here, so under the quirkiness your approach to new things is thoughtful and structured. You start slowly, set the rules, then commit. The earth-air friction in the card shows in how people read you. They're charmed by the ideas and then they wait to see whether you deliver. Capricorn and Aquarius sit next to each other in the zodiac, and people may pick up a small contradiction in you, the rebel who's actually quite conventional about money and deadlines. Fixed air doesn't like to adjust, so the card's constant shifting can look easier on you than it feels.

In a new job you're likely to be handed the odd project nobody else understands. In a community group it's setting up the spreadsheet and running the social nights. On a date you're interesting and a bit elusive. Next time you meet someone, give them one concrete detail about your week along with the big ideas.
rising.reversed:
Distracted and a bit remote is how Aquarius rising tends to look with this card reversed. You turn up with your mind on the other thing, or you've overcommitted to a group and it comes out as brisk, efficient coolness. People may read you as aloof when you're simply stretched.

New workplaces see it first, especially in meetings where you have good ideas and no time to follow them up. New friends may feel you're holding them at a polite distance. A date may leave unsure whether you liked them or just liked the conversation. A community project could slip because you're doing too much of it. Before the next new thing, cancel one commitment so you can arrive properly present, and make a point of asking the other person one question about themselves.

sun.upright:
Pisces is one of the two signs Jupiter rules, and this is Jupiter's card, so a Pisces Sun is hearing from its own ruler here, even if the ruler is calling from Capricorn, where it's in fall and hemmed in. You want to give, to imagine, to follow whatever moves you. The card wants that too, with a budget and a timetable attached.

Capricorn and Pisces are sextile, two signs apart, a cooperative link that still needs using. The card's earth and your water get on, the earth giving the water banks to run between, so it can give your dreams a practical form without crushing them. There's a foothold here as well. Jupiter rules the middle ten degrees of Pisces, the decan of the Nine of Cups, the card of the wish that comes true, and if your Sun is in that part of the sign the balancing act is closely tied to getting what you actually want. For any Pisces, mutable and changeable as the sign is, keeping more than one thing going comes naturally. Keeping track of them is harder, and you're a bit vague about money and you know it.

At work this is the creative job and the practical one, or a caring role alongside your own ambitions. With money it's knowing where it is at all. With a partner or a friend it's giving generously and having enough left over for yourself. Choose one practical system, a shared calendar or a separate savings account, and use it for three months without changing it.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun under the reversed card can drift. Too many commitments, too much given away, and the Jupiter that rules your sign gets generous past the point of sense. You've said yes to everyone's needs, and your own plans have slipped away without anyone noticing, including you. Sometimes you just stop answering, and the coins roll off somewhere quietly.

Money is often the first place, the bills unopened, the money lent to people who won't pay it back. Work comes next, with deadlines missed because you were helping someone else. Your energy may feel diffuse, as if you can't find the edges of yourself. Open the post, all of it, sit down with a friend who's good with numbers, and make one list of what you owe and what you're owed.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up the mood of every room. You feel what other people feel, sometimes before they do, and you need time alone to wring it all out. This card arrives with a busy, practical rhythm, and emotionally that could be exactly what helps, if you let it.

Jupiter rules Pisces, so the card is speaking with your Moon sign's own authority, and it's a gentle authority. Earth is kind to water, and in your inner weather that means something practical gives your feelings a shape. Folding the washing. Walking the dog. Making the soup you always make. The sextile between Capricorn and Pisces opens that door easily, though nobody can walk you through it. The tension is Jupiter's fall in Capricorn, the card's sign. The comfort on offer isn't the big dreamy kind. It's modest and structured, and part of you will find that a little disappointing. You may also have more in your hands than you realise, because you pick up other people's worries without noticing you've done it.

With sleep this is needing more of it than you think, and a proper wind-down before it. With friends it's being the one who listens and needing someone who listens back. Your body likes water, rest and a routine, and routine suits you better than you'd expect. Pick one daily habit with a clear end point, a set walk, a cup of tea at four, and keep it fixed.
moon.reversed:
Overwhelm with no obvious cause is common for a Pisces Moon when the card lands reversed. You're carrying everyone's feelings as well as your own practical load, and you can't tell any more which is which. The Jupiter that rules your sign tends to promise too much comfort to too many people, and then you need to hide for a day.

It shows in sleep, far too much or not nearly enough, and in a fuzzy, heavy feeling in the body. Friends may find you suddenly unavailable. A partner may get a sweet, vague version of you who agrees to everything and remembers none of it. Escapism creeps in, screens, sweets, one more episode. Take one evening to sort out only your own things, your own washing, your own emails, your own dinner, and let other people's needs wait until the morning.

rising.upright:
There's a softness to how Pisces rising meets people. You're easy to talk to, a bit dreamy, and strangers often feel you understand them before they've explained anything. Drawn for your mask, the Two of Pentacles gives that gentle manner a surprising competence, someone clearly holding a lot together while looking as if they're drifting through it.

Jupiter is your traditional chart ruler, because it rules Pisces, and this card is Jupiter at work in Capricorn, where it's in fall. So the card shows your ruler behaving with extra care, and people meet a more practical version of you than they expect. The sextile to Capricorn gives you an easy way to be taken seriously, if you use it. Your water and the card's earth work well together, and on your face that comes across as warmth that's also dependable. Pisces is mutable and you adapt almost too readily, shifting your manner to suit whoever's in front of you. The card rewards that, up to a point. The Nine of Cups decan, Jupiter's slice of the middle of Pisces, can add a contented, well-looked-after air to the first impression.

Starting somewhere new, you're the kind one who turns out to be very good at the work. With new friends it's being both the listener and the one who remembers to book the table. In dating you seem gentle and turn out to be harder to pin down than people think. Next time someone asks what you do, give them the practical answer first.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with the card reversed tends to look vague. You turn up late or on the wrong day, apologise sweetly, and people forgive you, but they file it away. The Jupiter that rules your rising sign is generous with yeses, and its fall in Capricorn means the follow-through lags behind them. Or the gentleness becomes a way of dodging the practical questions, and strangers are left unsure whether you've agreed to anything.

It shows most in work and money, in first meetings where you're lovely and don't follow up, and with landlords or banks who need a clear answer. New friends may get cancellations. A date could leave not knowing if you're interested. Put every arrangement in writing for a while, a quick message confirming the time and place, sent straight after you've agreed to it.

1.upright:
Your body, your bearing and the way you start things all belong to the first house, along with the face you walk out the door with. With the Two of Pentacles here you may feel a lot like the figure on the card, moving between roles all day and adjusting your footing as you go. The parent and the employee, the carer and the person with plans of their own, all before breakfast.

Aries is the first house's natural sign, and Capricorn squares Aries, cardinal against cardinal, a friction that forces things to happen. You'll feel it as impatience with yourself, a sense that you should be getting on with your own life while you're busy keeping everyone else's going. The card's earth has no quarrel with this fiery house and no natural ease there either, so the steady, practical approach has to be chosen. It won't just arrive.
